clue.text: Singer in musical, touring

indicators.note: 'in' tells the solver the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning a word break

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A performer goes on tour with a stage musical.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice range.

clue.text: Mysterious man, man of the church

blocks.note: arch means knowing, slyly mischievous
a bishop is a chess piece, and chess pieces are called men

explanation.surface: An enigmatic figure turns out to be a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'man' misleads: the first is a chessman, the second part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An archbishop is a senior cleric ranking above bishops in a church hierarchy.

clue.text: One giving better advice?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone whose counsel is superior to others'
setter's reading: a better is one who bets, so this is someone advising gamblers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as the comparative of good, but here it is a noun: a person who places bets.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipster sells or offers predictions to people gambling on races and other events.

clue.text: No PR in Central American country for international award

indicators.note: 'in' places the two letters inside the name of the country that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
Belize is a country in Central America
taken as written, the abbreviation for public relations

explanation.surface: A Central American nation is denied publicity ahead of a global prize.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nobel Prizes are awarded internationally each year for achievements in science, literature and peace.

clue.text: Peculiar periodic social event

blocks.note: odd as in occasional, now and then, as in 'the odd visit'
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A strange gathering held every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, oddball describes something eccentric or strange.

clue.text: Non-stop, but with no purpose?

blocks.note: first meaning: never ceasing
second, cryptic meaning: an end is an aim, so lacking one is to be without an aim

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading, which splits the word into its parts: an end is a goal, and -less means without.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never stops is limitless; read literally, the word means lacking a goal.

clue.text: Christmas show character - I metamorphose spookily around end of Aladdin

indicators.note: doing something spookily is doing it weirdly, so the letters come out in an eerie new order
only the final letter of the named word is taken
the jumbled letters are set to surround the single letter

blocks.note: taken as written, for rearranging
the last letter of the pantomime title

explanation.surface: An actor in a Christmas show announces an eerie transformation during Aladdin.
explanation.walkthrough: Pantomime is the British Christmas-season family theatre, with shows like Aladdin; the jumbled letters wrap round the N.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime horse, two actors in one costume, is a stock comic figure in these festive stage shows.

clue.text: One with a cold manner in charge on English mountain

blocks.note: IC is the abbreviation for in charge
E is the abbreviation for English
berg is a mountain, as in the South African word

explanation.surface: A frosty person is put in command on a peak in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, an iceberg is a person who is aloof and emotionally chilly.

clue.text: Docked in good time for nobleman

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the final letter is removed

blocks.note: arriving in good time is arriving ahead of schedule

explanation.surface: A boat moored promptly, carrying an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer ranking between a marquess and a viscount.

clue.text: Painter in quiet little avenue met Tristan unexpectedly

indicators.note: something turning out unexpectedly comes out in an unforeseen order

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
Ave is the short form of avenue
taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: An artist on a quiet little street happens upon Tristan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Painter' could be any artist; the anagram fixes the street-side kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavement artist draws pictures in chalk on the sidewalk, usually for coins from passers-by.

clue.text: Policeman left with US composer

blocks.note: a cop is a police officer
L is the abbreviation for left
and joins things, as with does

explanation.surface: An officer departs in the company of an American musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron Copland was an American composer, known for Appalachian Spring and Fanfare for the Common Man.

clue.text: Nursed a poorly man like Fonteyn's partner?

indicators.note: something poorly is in bad shape, so the letters are out of their proper order

blocks.note: taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: A sick man was cared for, perhaps the ballerina's dance partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Margot Fonteyn's famous partner was Rudolf Nureyev, a male ballet dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: Danseur is the French-derived term for a male ballet dancer, the role Nureyev filled.

clue.text: Subject to its value, how books may be bought in addition?

blocks.clueFragment: Subject to its value, how books may be bought
blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: a book token is spent on books up to its face value
second meaning: likewise, for the same reason

explanation.walkthrough: A book token is a gift voucher exchangeable for books, popular in Britain; the phrase is read literally for the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom introduces a further point that follows equally, much like also or similarly.

clue.text: Betray radicals in the rank and file

blocks.note: to grass is British slang for informing on someone
radical comes from the Latin for root; in maths a radical is a root

explanation.surface: Extremists in the ordinary membership are informed upon.
explanation.definitionFit: The grass roots are the ordinary members of a party or movement, as opposed to its leaders.

clue.text: Dreamlike, a 50 after county side comes up short

indicators.note: falling short means missing the end, so the last letter goes
'after' puts the first pieces behind the county piece

blocks.note: Surrey is a county south of London, and also its county cricket side
taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A cricket team scores a half-century but still falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county that fields a county cricket team; 'a 50' sounds like a batting score.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal means bizarre and irrational, with the strange quality of a dream.

clue.text: 26, perhaps, eating last of fruit cocktail

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one piece swallows the other
only the final letter of the following word is used

blocks.note: 26-across is a bass, which is one kind of singer
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fish, perhaps, eating the remains of a fruit cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the fish, but its other meaning, a deep male voice, is the one needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinger is a mixed drink of brandy and white crème de menthe.

clue.text: Said about part circling a large city

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so the first word goes around the second

blocks.note: oral means spoken
a bit is a part or piece

explanation.surface: A section said to ring a big metropolis.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbital road is a ring road around a city, as the M25 encircles London.

clue.text: Money that is found in old wood

blocks.note: brass is British slang for money
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Cash discovered in an ancient forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wood' means not a forest but a golf club with a wooden head.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassie was a traditional golf club, equivalent to the modern two-wood.

clue.text: Toboggan full of crack in suitcases

indicators.note: something full of another thing holds it inside

blocks.note: a luge is a racing sled
a crack is a wisecrack, a joke

explanation.surface: A sled crammed with something cracked inside some cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage is the collective word for bags and cases taken on a journey.

clue.text: Mother's broken flask

indicators.note: a broken thing is in pieces that can be put together differently

blocks.note: taken as written, the possessive S included

explanation.surface: Mum's vacuum flask has been smashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Thermos is the brand name that became the general word for a vacuum flask.

clue.text: Young child in red, told off

indicators.note: 'off' suggests going wrong or bad, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: A little one dressed in red gets scolded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told off' reads as scolded, but 'told' belongs to the fodder and 'off' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A toddler is a child just learning to walk, typically one to three years old.

clue.text: Wise man's headgear held by mother

indicators.note: being held by something means sitting within its grasp

blocks.note: mama is a familiar word for mother
a hat is headgear

explanation.surface: A sage's cap is kept by his mum.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma, Sanskrit for great soul, is an Indian title of reverence for a sage, as with Gandhi.

clue.text: Generous supporter of mayor righted wrong

indicators.note: putting something wrong means getting it into the incorrect order

blocks.note: taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: A benefactor of the mayor puts a wrong to rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporter of mayor' looks like the definition; 'of' belongs to the fodder instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy godmother, from Cinderella, is anyone who unexpectedly provides help or money.

clue.text: Prophet, a second son

blocks.note: taken as written
a mo is a moment, a second
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A seer and his younger boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos was a Hebrew prophet, with a book of the Old Testament named after him.

clue.text: Chaotic state of affairs in a Sicilian port

blocks.note: a mess is a disorderly situation
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Things are in disarray in a harbour town in Sicily.
explanation.definitionFit: Messina is a port city in north-east Sicily, on the strait facing mainland Italy.

clue.text: Country hotel, so in need of refurbishment

indicators.note: something needing refurbishment must be rebuilt and put back together differently

blocks.note: taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: A rural inn so run down it needs doing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country hotel' reads as one phrase, but 'Country' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a landlocked kingdom entirely surrounded by South Africa.

clue.text: Dear dessert? Pity

blocks.note: in Britain a sweet is a pudding or dessert
heart means compassion, as in 'have a heart'

explanation.surface: An expensive pudding is a shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear dessert' suggests a costly pudding; 'Dear' is a term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are affectionate forms of address for a loved one.

clue.text: Fish, black when small

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
as can mean while or when
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A fish that is dark while it is young.
explanation.definitionFit: The bass is a spiny-finned fish caught both in the sea and in fresh water.
